![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14221452/assets/1628d71e973666b1b79aa5e86a9fa4b7cc8fffec93778bde92db7b3600bd13f5.png)

Find the area enclosed by the curve (shown above) defined parametrically as

$$
x={t}^{2}-4,\,y={t}^{3}-4t,\,t\in (-2,2).
$$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-4)=2t.
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}({t}^{3}-4t)\cdot 2t\,\text{d}t \\  & =2{\int }_{-2}^{2}({t}^{4}-4{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a negative number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\le 0$ for all $t\in (-2,2).$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =2{\int }_{-2}^{2}({t}^{4}-4{t}^{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\cdot {\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}|}_{-2}^{2}-8\cdot {\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =2(\frac{32}{5}+\frac{32}{5})-8(\frac{8}{3}+\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =\frac{128}{5}-\frac{128}{3} \\  & =-\frac{256}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required area is $|-\frac{256}{15}|=\frac{256}{15}.$
